title: NEW CLAY COUNTY ROYALTY
full_story:
The Clay County Fair wrapped up Friday night with the Clay County Fair Queen Pageant.

Your 2026 Miss Clay County Fair is Landree Erwin the 21-year-old daughter of Brent and Chrissy Erwin of Louisville.  Olivia Haun is the retiring Miss Clay County Fair.

Taking the title of 1st runner up and Peoples Choice award winner was Kamry Austin, the 20-year-old daughter of Shane and Rachel Walker of Flora and Nick Austin of Fairfield.  2nd runner up, was Laila Smith, the 16-year-old daughter of Dustin and Kathy Smith of Louisville.

The Physical Fitness Award and Miss Photogenic was Madison Winterowd, the 20-year-old daughter of Matt and Amanda Winterowd of Louisville.  The Stage Presence Award winner was Lucy Clark, the 21-year-old daughter of Brad and Mandy Clark of Louisville, and the Legacy Sparkplug Award winner and Miss Congeniality was Elizabetha Hagen, the 19-year-old daughter of Derek and Melissa Hagen of Clay City.

The 2026 Little Miss Clay County Fair is Kylie Noll the daughter of Jordan and Amanda Noll crowned on Monday night, and the New JR Miss Clay County Fair is Maura Kay Smith the daughter of Dustin and Kathy Smith who was crowned on Tuesday night.

title: KINMUNDY ACCIDENT
full_story:
Friday morning the Marion County Sheriff’s Department reported that an 82-year-old Kinmundy man fell 20 feet off a ladder into a rock driveway in rural Salem.

Initial reports indicate the man, whose name has not been released, was standing on a ladder cutting down a tree limb when it began to fall and swung towards the ladder knocking the man to the ground.

The accident occurred at a home on Hester Lane near Cross Road at around 9:40 Friday morning.

title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The board reviewed estimates for the lift station on second street, the repair estimate was $3,864.49, and the replacement estimate was $7,192.10.  The board voted to repair the lift station.

The Board reviewed information regarding the Municipal Clerks Institute and Academy, a three-year professional development program consisting of approximately 38 to 40 hours of annual in-person instruction with an option to pursue the Master Academy for IIMC-approved continuing education.  Estimated cost of the three-year program and Master Academy is $2,500.00.  Trustee approved Village Clerk Cindy Manuel’s attendance.

Trustees again discussed nuisance properties.  Trustee Gary Ulm moved to authorize the Village to proceed with mowing properties that remain in violation if the property owners have not abated the nuisance.  The Village will follow all procedures outlined in the Village Nuisance Ordinance.

Residents were reminded that the Noble Chowder is scheduled for Saturday, beginning at 11:00 am and Village-wide garage sales are scheduled for Saturday, August 15th.

title: FCCO ARRESTED
full_story:
A Fayette County Sheriff’s Office Correctional Deputy was arrested in connection with allegations of sexual misconduct involving an inmate in the Fayette County Jail.

The sheriff’s office reported that, after learning of the allegations on July 29th, the administration immediately transferred the inmate to another correctional facility, and the deputy was arrested, charged, and transferred to another county jail for holding.

To maintain transparency and eliminate any conflict of interest, the Fayette County Sheriff’s Office immediately contacted Illinois State Police Investigations and requested they lead the investigation into the allegations.

The Fayette County Sheriff’s Office, in a release, says it takes all allegations of staff misconduct with the utmost seriousness, with a priority of maintaining a safe, secure environment and upholding the public trust.  The name of the correctional officer and the inmate are not being released at this time to protect the integrity of the active investigation.

title: FCC STUDENTS EXCEL
full_story:
Forty-three Frontier Community College student-athletes were named to the 2025–26 NJCAA All-Academic Teams in recognition of their exceptional performance in the classroom.

Student-athletes named to the NJCAA All-Academic First Team achieved a perfect 4.00 grade-point average.  Second Team honorees earned GPAs between 3.80 and 3.99, while Third Team honorees posted GPAs between 3.60 and 3.79.  Frontier had 19 student-athletes named to the First Team, 16 selected for the Second Team and eight recognized on the Third Team.

In addition to the individual honors, all three Frontier Community College athletic teams ranked among the top six nationally in their respective sports for academic performance.

The Bobcats volleyball team ranked third in the nation with an overall GPA of 3.84.  The baseball team tied for fifth with a 3.74 GPA, while the softball team finished sixth with a 3.79 GPA.

Frontier Community College Athletic Director Jeremy Ellis praised the student-athletes for their dedication in the classroom after the NJCAA released the results.

Ellis also emphasized the important roles Frontier faculty, staff, administrators and community members play in helping student-athletes succeed.

“We want to recognize the people working behind the scenes,” Ellis said.  “Our faculty, staff and administration are very supportive of us.  They do a great job working with our student-athletes and making themselves available when help is needed.  The hard work our student-athletes are putting in is also paying off, and these results show that.”

Ellis said the support student-athletes receive from the Fairfield community also contributes to their success.

The NJCAA All-Academic Teams program recognizes student-athletes from across the country for their commitment to academic excellence while competing in collegiate athletics.

title: FAYETTE COUNTY INVESTIGATION
full_story:
The Fayette County Coroner’s Office was called out to a location near Farina on Wednesday evening.

A body who was later identified as 40-year-old Antwan D. Johnson of the Chicago area, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.  Johnson was pronounced dead at the scene.  Assisting at the scene that evening were the Fayette County Sheriff’s Office and the Farina First Responders.

Fayette County Coroner Dave Harris had contact with the Harvey, Illinois Police Department about the body.  Harris was informed that Johnson was being investigated there in regard to two murdered victims.

An autopsy on Johnson was performed in Springfield on Friday.

Now joining the investigation of Johnson’s death along with the Fayette County Coroner’s Office and the Fayette County Sheriff’s Office is the Harvey Police Department and the CSI division of the Illinois State Police.

title: LAKE LAND FULL-TIME HONORS
full_story:
Lake Land College announced that more than 800 full-time students earned academic honors for the 2026 Spring semester.

To qualify for the President’s List, a student must have completed at least 12 credit hours in courses numbered 040 or higher per semester, excluding summer term, with a GPA of 3.8 – 4.0.  Making the President’s List locally was Chelci Irvin of Louisville.

To qualify for the Dean’s List, a student must have completed at least 12 credit hours in courses numbered 040 or higher per semester, excluding summer term, with a GPA of 3.65 – 3.79.  Making the Dean’s List locally were Blake West of Louisville, and Brooke Koelm of Edgewood.

To qualify for the Honor’s List, a student must have completed at least 12 hours in courses numbered 040 or higher per semester, excluding summer term, with a GPA of 3.5 – 3.64.  Making the Honor’s List locally were Miah Ballard and Shelly Pierson of Louisville, and Madison Tonn of Edgewood.

title: RITA FRAZER HALL OF FAME INDUCTEE
full_story:
RFD Radio Network’s Rita Frazer was selected as a 2026 inductee into the National Association of Farm Broadcasting (NAFB) Hall of Fame.

Frazer, who has more than 35 years of agricultural broadcasting experience, currently serves as audio news manager for the Illinois Farm Bureau’s marketing and communications division.  Frazer previously served as network anchor/broadcast editor at WSMI Radio in Litchfield.  She joined the staff there in January 1990 and served local farmers and the mid-Illinois community for 22 years.

She joined the RFD Radio Network full time in 2011.  “It has been an honor to serve farmers and tell the story of Illinois agriculture. It’s a blessing,” Frazer said.  “Being recognized by my peers with the Hall of Fame award is truly an honor, and humbling.”

A past president and 35-year member of NAFB, Frazer has earned numerous accolades, including the 2024 NAFB Farm Broadcaster of the Year Award.  In addition to serving as NAFB president, Frazer also was NAFB East Region vice president for two years.

Frazer will be recognized November 19th at the 83rd NAFB Convention in Kansas City, Missouri, along with Tom Cassidy, who recently retired as farm director and general manager at Ag Radio Network in Barneveld, New York.

“Rita and Tom have been trusted voices for agriculture for decades, delivering the news and information that farmers and ranchers depend on every day,” said Don Wick, president and owner of the Red River Farm Network and chair of the 2026 NAFB Hall of Fame Committee.  “Their leadership has helped shape the future of our association and our industry, making them truly deserving of this recognition.  We are delighted to honor them as this year’s inductees.”
